findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable by any process or user on the instance and by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, and it is stored unencrypted in the Terraform state and version control, leaking long-lived IAM credentials.

Ingress on TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressable instance to the entire internet for brute-force and exploitation attempts. Combined with the public subnet and the credentials in user data, a successful login yields AWS API access.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled (http_tokens is 'optional'). On an internet-facing web server this allows a simple SSRF or command-injection flaw to read instance metadata and user data — which here contains hard-coded AWS keys — without any token.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root EBS volume is created unencrypted and data at rest (including the credentials baked into user data) is unprotected.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), leaving all data stored on the attached volume unencrypted at rest.

The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and therefore is itself unencrypted. Snapshots are independently shareable/copyable artifacts, so an unencrypted snapshot is a durable, easily exfiltrated copy of the volume's data.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with a route table default route to the internet gateway means every instance launched here, including web_host, receives a public IP and is directly reachable from the internet with no bastion or load balancer boundary.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with a route table that has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway causes any future workload placed in this subnet to be exposed directly to the internet by default.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data provisions plain Apache with no TLS listener, so all traffic to the web host is transmitted in cleartext and subject to interception or modification.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound segmentation. A compromised instance can freely exfiltrate data or reach command-and-control infrastructure.
The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network telemetry (source/destination IPs, ports, accepted/rejected traffic) is stored unencrypted.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy accompanies this bucket, so an accidental ACL or policy change could expose VPC flow log data publicly. There is also no policy requiring aws:SecureTransport, permitting cleartext HTTP access to objects.
